captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/29_ijepa, specifically its ViT step 1 (models/vision_transformer.py, masks/multiblock.py, data/imagenet.py, utils/schedulers.py, train_ijepa.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Assran et al. (2023) I-JEPA, following facebookresearch/ijepa. I-JEPA ships its OWN Vision Transformer (models/vision_transformer.py -- measured: it imports only torch, NOT timm) and trains from scratch on ImageNet-1k, so this ports self-contained and torch-only. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (29) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
paper.authors: Assran, Duval, Misra, Bojanowski, Vincent, Rabbat, LeCun, Ballas

scope: The ViT step 1 is ported: a context encoder (a VisionTransformer with no CLS token) sees a large context block of patches; a narrow predictor (a shallow ViT) predicts the representations of several masked target blocks; the targets come from an EMA target encoder (a momentum copy of the context encoder, no gradient), layer-normalised, and the loss is a smooth-L1 in latent space averaged over the target blocks. Multi-block masking (1 context block, 4 target blocks) is generated by a collate_fn. AdamW under cosine LR and weight-decay schedules with linear warmup; the EMA momentum follows a cosine schedule (0.996 -> 1.0); gradient-norm clipping. The capture's unified step 2 (ViT-B/16) is also ported additively (recipe: unified); see rewritten_during_the_port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the target ViT encoder (target_encoder.*, the prefix stripped so it loads straight into a plain VisionTransformer): the patch-embed conv, the learnable position embedding, the transformer blocks and the final norm, producing the mean-pooled patch feature (embed_dim; 1280 for vit_huge, 48 for the smoke's vit_tiny). The context encoder (encoder.*), the predictor (predictor.*) and the mask token are training machinery and are excluded. The target encoder (not the context encoder) is shipped -- it is the representation I-JEPA is evaluated on (the capture's own linear eval uses the target_encoder key).
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the target ViT encoder's mean-pooled patch tokens (embed_dim; I-JEPA has no CLS token), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation I-JEPA trains with). The capture's own eval trains an AdamW linear head; this port follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: the ViT step 1 (native ViT-H/14) is ported, and the capture's unified step 2 (ViT-B/16) is added additively, selected by a recipe: unified key in train (absent == the native step-1 path, unchanged)

the unified step 2 needed NO separate trainer: train_pretrain_ijepa.py already implements the recipe -- it uses the lr directly (the capture baked lr=1.5e-4*1024/256=6e-4 into the config, so nothing is rescaled), builds the arch named in the config (vit_base is one of its builders), reads augmentation: step2 from the config, and its cosine weight-decay is constant when weight_decay == final_wd. The only addition is a guarded milestone checkpoint: it writes checkpoint_epoch_{N}.pth at each training.save_at_epochs, a block that is empty for the native config (which never sets that key), so native behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. Duplicating the loop into a second file to add two lines would have been a second copy of one rule

the adapter gained a recipe: unified branch (disjoint key sets: native-only use_horizontal_flip, which step-2 augmentation ignores, vs unified-only save_at_epochs) and, for the unified recipe, extracts encoder_epoch{N}.pt (the target encoder) at each milestone so the 100/200/300 sweep can probe each; configs/pretrain_vit.yaml (recipe: unified, ViT-B/16) and configs/linear_eval_vit.yaml (name vit_base) are added

I-JEPA's own vision_transformer.py is ported (torch-only, no timm); the port adds a vit_tiny arch and builds the predictor with pred_num_heads = max(1, pred_dim // 64) so a small hermetic CPU smoke can run at a lower resolution with a narrow predictor

the multi-block mask collator, the context/target encoders, the narrow predictor, the layer-normed latent targets and the smooth-L1 loss are kept faithfully (all torch); the EMA target update and the cosine LR / weight-decay / EMA schedules are kept
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called .cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch); the DataLoader gets a seeded generator

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, the bf16 autocast, the gradient accumulation / no_sync and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32
